items.set_statement_mirror: For $n=2$ or $3$, let $X=\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}$ and let $X^{an}$ be its complex analytic space. Define analytification by $\mathcal F^{an}=\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_{X^{an}}$. It is an exact tensor-compatible equivalence from algebraic coherent sheaves (locally finitely presented $\mathcal O_X$-modules) to holomorphic coherent sheaves. It identifies algebraic and holomorphic morphisms, preserves cohomology and the derived morphism groups $\operatorname{Ext}^q$, and commutes with restriction to the fixed hyperplane $L_\infty=\{z_0=0\}$. For an algebraic coherent sheaf $\mathcal E$ flat over a finite-type complex parameter scheme $S$, let $p:X\times S\to S$ be projection. Analytification commutes with the algebraic family structure and fiber restrictions. Whenever the algebraic and analytic higher direct images $R^qp_*\mathcal E$ are locally free and the natural maps from their residue-field fibers to $H^q(X_s,\mathcal E_s)$ are isomorphisms, the comparison identifies those direct images and base-change maps. No assertion is made that an arbitrary holomorphic family over a nonproper algebraic base algebraizes.

citations_from_current_source.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field and $n\ge0$, let
$S=k[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ be graded by total degree with $\deg x_i=1$, let
$\mathbb P^n_k=\operatorname{Proj}S$ with twisting sheaves
$\mathcal O(d)=\widetilde{S(d)}$, and let $F$ be a coherent
$\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n_k}$-module. Then there is a finitely generated graded
$S$-module $M$ with $\widetilde M\cong F$ and an exact sequence of graded
$S$-modules with degree-preserving maps
$$0\longrightarrow F_{n+1}\longrightarrow F_n\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow F_0\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow 0$$
in which every $F_i$ is a finite direct sum of shifted free modules $S(d)$
with $d\in\mathbb Z$, and whose sheafification
$$0\longrightarrow\widetilde F_{n+1}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow\widetilde F_0\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow 0$$
is an exact sequence of $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n_k}$-modules in which every
$\widetilde F_i$ is a finite direct sum $\bigoplus_j\mathcal O(d_{ij})$ of
twisting sheaves. The resolution has length at most $n+1$: the displayed free
terms $F_0,\dots,F_{n+1}$ are finite direct sums of shifted free modules, any
of them may be zero, a shorter resolution is allowed when it terminates
earlier, and the truncation degree of $M$ is chosen so that $M$ is finitely
generated and $\widetilde M\cong F$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a commutative
ring with $1$ ([[def-commutative-ring]]), let $n\ge0$, let $d\in\mathbb Z$ and
let $X=\mathbb P^n_A\cong\operatorname{Proj}A[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ be relative
projective space ([[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]],
[[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]]), with twisting sheaf
$\mathcal O_X(d)$ ([[def-twisting-sheaf-proj]]) and cohomology
$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$. Then
$$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0\qquad\text{unless }q=0\text{ or }q=n.$$
If $n>0$, then $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ when $d\ge0$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0$ when $d<0$, where
$A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ is the degree-$d$ graded piece
([[def-graded-ring-and-graded-module]]); and $H^n(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$ is the
free $A$-module on the Laurent monomials $x_0^{e_0}\cdots x_n^{e_n}$ with
$e_i<0$ for every $i$ and $\sum_ie_i=d$, so that it is nonzero precisely when
$d\le-n-1$ and $A\ne0$. For $n=0$ one has $\mathbb P^0_A=\operatorname{Spec}A$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A$ for every $d\in\mathbb Z$, with all higher
groups zero. The zero ring $A=0$ is allowed: then $X=\varnothing$ and all
groups are zero, in agreement with both displayed descriptions.

citations_from_current_source.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited suppliers
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a Noetherian commutative ring with $1$,
let $X$ be a scheme projective over $A$ in the finite-dimensional
H-projective convention ([[def-projective-morphism-pre-proj]]): the structure
morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ factors as a closed immersion
$X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^N_A$ followed by the projection, for some $N\ge0$
([[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]]). Let $L$ be an ample
invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module ([[def-ample-invertible-sheaf]],
[[def-invertible-sheaf]]) and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent
$\mathcal O_X$-module ([[def-coherent-module-scheme]]). Then there is an
integer $m_0$ such that
$$H^q\bigl(X,\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}L^{\otimes m}\bigr)=0$$
for every $q>0$ and every integer $m\ge m_0$, with a single bound $m_0$
working simultaneously for all $q$; here $H^q$ is sheaf cohomology
([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]) and $L^{\otimes m}$ is the
$m$-fold tensor power ([[def-twist-quasi-coherent-sheaf-projective]]). The
empty scheme $X$, the empty base $\operatorname{Spec}A=\varnothing$, the zero
ring $A=0$, the zero module $\mathcal F=0$ and the case of an ample $L$ with
$\mathcal O(1)$ already very ample for a power $L^{\otimes d}$ with $d=1$ are
included. No effectivity of $m_0$ is claimed.

Let
$$\cdots \to A_{n-1} \to A_n \to A_{n+1} \to A_{n+2} \to A_{n+3} \to \cdots$$
and
$$\cdots \to B_{n-1} \to B_n \to B_{n+1} \to B_{n+2} \to B_{n+3} \to \cdots$$
be long exact sequences in an abelian category, together with a morphism of
these sequences. If the four comparison maps at $A_{n-1},A_n,A_{n+2},A_{n+3}$
are isomorphisms, then the comparison map $A_{n+1} \to B_{n+1}$ is an
isomorphism.

citations_from_current_source.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, and let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space. Then
the abelian category $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules has
enough injectives: every $\mathcal O_X$-module embeds into an injective
$\mathcal O_X$-module, and the functorial injective embedding supplied by the
Grothendieck injective-embedding theorem for Grothendieck categories supplies,
by iteration of cokernels, one specific injective resolution
$$0\to\mathcal F\to I^0(\mathcal F)\to I^1(\mathcal F)\to\cdots$$
to each $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ with no further selection
([[def-injective-resolution-in-an-abelian-category]]). The Axiom of Choice
enters exactly through that embedding theorem applied to
$\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$; the category-theoretic verification below is
choice-free.

citations_from_current_source.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, let $X$ be a topological space and let
$\mathcal F$ be a flasque sheaf of abelian groups on $X$
([[def-flasque-sheaf]]). Then for every open subspace $U\subseteq X$ and every
integer $q>0$,
$$H^q(U,\mathcal F|_U)=0,$$
where $H^q(U,-)$ denotes sheaf cohomology on the space $U$
([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]) computed with the global
sections functor of $U$, and $\mathcal F|_U$ is the restriction of $\mathcal F$
to $U$. Equivalently, every restriction $\mathcal F|_U$ is $\Gamma$-acyclic
([[def-acyclic-sheaf-global-sections]]).

Assume the Axiom of Dependent Choice.

Let $I$ be a supplied injective resolution datum on a class $\mathcal D$, let
$F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an additive left exact functor, and let
$$0\to A\to J^0\to J^1\to J^2\to\cdots$$
be an $F$-acyclic resolution of $A$ relative to $I$. Assume moreover that
$A\in\mathcal D$ and that, for $Z^0:=A$ and
$$0\to Z^q\to J^q\to Z^{q+1}\to0\qquad(q\ge0),$$
each $Z^q$ lies in $\mathcal D$. Then for every $n\ge 0$ there is a canonical
isomorphism
$$R_I^nF(A)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^n(F(J^\bullet_{\mathrm{del}})).$$

citations_from_current_source.quote:
Let $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be a morphism of sheaves of sets on a
topological space $X$, and let $I$ be the **presheaf image**
$$I(U):=\varphi_U(\mathcal F(U))\subseteq\mathcal G(U).$$
Define the **image sheaf** $J$ by
$$ J(U):=\left\{\,t\in\mathcal G(U): \text{ for every }x\in U\text{ there exists }x\in V\subseteq U \text{ and }s\in\mathcal F(V)\text{ with }\varphi_V(s)=t|_V\,\right\}. $$
Then $J$ is a subsheaf of $\mathcal G$, $\varphi$ factors through $J$, and the
canonical map
$$aI\longrightarrow J$$
is an isomorphism. In particular, the image sheaf is the sheafification of the
objectwise image presheaf.

citations_from_current_source.quote:
Let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf on a topological space $X$, let
$\eta_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F\to a\mathcal F$ be its sheafification map, and let
$\mathcal G$ be a sheaf on $X$. Then every morphism of presheaves
$$\varphi:\mathcal F\longrightarrow\mathcal G$$
factors uniquely through $\eta_{\mathcal F}$:
there is a unique morphism of sheaves
$$\overline\varphi:a\mathcal F\longrightarrow\mathcal G$$
such that
$$\varphi=\overline\varphi\circ\eta_{\mathcal F}.$$

Let $(f,f^\sharp):(X,\mathcal O_X)\to(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed
spaces and let $\mathcal F$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-module
([[def-module-on-ringed-space]]). The direct image presheaf
$f_*\mathcal F$ is defined on opens $V\subseteq Y$ by
$(f_*\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(f^{-1}(V))$
([[def-direct-image-sheaf]]); when $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of modules, this
presheaf is again a sheaf of modules on $Y$
([[lem-direct-image-is-sheaf]]), and for a morphism of ringed spaces it is an
$\mathcal O_Y$-module, because $f_*$ is right adjoint to the inverse image
functor $f^*$ on modules ([[thm-pullback-pushforward-module-adjunction]]); a
right adjoint is left exact and additive
([[cor-a-right-adjoint-is-left-exact-and-a-left-adjoint-is-right-exact]]).

Fix the supplied functorial injective resolution datum $I$ on
$\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ of
[[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]]: it assigns to every
$\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ one specific injective resolution
$0\to\mathcal F\to I^0(\mathcal F)\to I^1(\mathcal F)\to\cdots$
([[def-injective-resolution-in-an-abelian-category]]) with deleted complex
$I(\mathcal F)_{\mathrm{del}}$
([[def-right-derived-object-relative-to-injective-resolution-data]]). For
every $q\in\mathbb Z$ define the **$q$-th higher direct image sheaf**

$$R^qf_*\mathcal F:=R_I^qf_*(\mathcal F)=H^q\bigl(f_*I(\mathcal F)_{\mathrm{del}}\bigr),$$

the $q$-th right derived object of the additive left exact functor
$f_*:\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)\to\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y)$ relative to the
fixed datum $I$ ([[def-right-derived-object-relative-to-injective-resolution-data]]),
the cohomology object being taken in the abelian category of
$\mathcal O_Y$-modules. We also keep the convention $R^qf_*\mathcal F=0$ for
$q<0$.

By the derived-object convention this makes $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ a specific
$\mathcal O_Y$-module for every $\mathcal F$ and $q$, depending on the fixed
datum $I$; in degree zero the left exactness of $f_*$ supplies a canonical
natural isomorphism $R^0f_*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}f_*\mathcal F$
([[thm-zero-th-right-derived-functor-of-a-left-exact-functor-recovers-the-functor]],
which assumes the Axiom of Dependent Choice
([[def-dependent-choice]])), so the $q=0$ term is the ordinary direct image.
The Axiom of Choice supplies the functorial injective resolution datum of
$\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and implies the
Dependent Choice required by the cited degree-zero and comparison theorems
([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]). If $J$ is any other supplied injective resolution
datum on $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$, then the functors $R_I^qf_*$ and
$R_J^qf_*$ are naturally isomorphic
([[thm-right-derived-functors-from-two-supplied-injective-resolution-data-are-naturally-isomorphic]]),
so the higher direct image is independent of the resolution up to a canonical
comparison isomorphism.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, let $X$ be a topological space with supplied
functorial injective resolution datum $I_X$ and sheaf cohomology
$H^q(X,-)$ as in [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]].

1. (Covariance in the sheaf.) Every morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$
   of abelian sheaves on $X$ induces additive maps
   $H^q(X,\varphi):H^q(X,\mathcal F)\to H^q(X,\mathcal G)$, and
   $\mathcal F\mapsto H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ is a covariant additive functor.
2. (Contravariance in the space.) Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, let
   $\mathcal G$ be an abelian sheaf on $Y$, let $\mathcal F$ be an abelian sheaf on $X$, and let
   $\varphi:f^{-1}\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ be a morphism of abelian sheaves. Then there are maps
   $$H^q(Y,\mathcal G)\longrightarrow H^q(X,\mathcal F)\qquad(q\ge0)$$
   depending only on $\varphi$, natural in $\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal F$, and in
   degree $0$ the map is the composite
   $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal G)\to\Gamma(X,f^{-1}\mathcal G)\xrightarrow{\ \Gamma(X,\varphi)\ }\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$
   of section pullback with $\varphi$; for composable data
   $g:Y\to Z$, $\psi:g^{-1}\mathcal H\to\mathcal G$,
   $\varphi:f^{-1}\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ the map of the composite pair
   $\varphi\circ f^{-1}\psi:(gf)^{-1}\mathcal H\to\mathcal F$ is the composite of
   the two maps (compatibility with compositions).

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a commutative
ring and let $n\ge0$ be an integer, and let $\mathbb P^n_A$ be the projective
space over $A$ with its standard charts
([[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]]). Then every
quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n_A}$-module $\mathcal F$
([[def-quasi-coherent-module-scheme]]) satisfies
$$H^q(\mathbb P^n_A,\mathcal F)=0$$
for every integer $q>n$, where $H^q$ is sheaf cohomology
([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]) applied to the underlying
sheaf of abelian groups of $\mathcal F$ ([[def-module-on-ringed-space]]). The
case $n=0$ is included; the zero ring $A=0$ is allowed, and then
$\mathbb P^n_A=\varnothing$.

derivations_from_current_source.claim: At a complex point, coherent algebraic and analytic modules are finite-dimensional complex vector spaces, so the absolute assertions hold in dimension zero. Flatness in [A1] makes analytification exact stalkwise, including for nonreduced finite-type schemes. Tensor associativity gives tensor compatibility and compatibility with quotient restriction to a hyperplane. A finite algebraic presentation analytifies to a finite analytic presentation, so [A3] ensures its cokernel is coherent. For a closed analytic embedding, direct image is exact on stalks and preserves flabby sheaves: its sections over an open are the original sections over the intersection with the closed subspace. Pushing forward a flabby resolution therefore identifies cohomology on the closed subspace and its direct image. These facts apply to the hyperplane sequences below.

Suppose the absolute theorem has been proved in dimensions below $r$, where $1\le r\le3$. For $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}$ the natural comparison is an isomorphism by [A5] and [F3]. The exact hyperplane sequences $0\to\mathcal O(m-1)\xrightarrow{x_0}\mathcal O(m)\to i_*\mathcal O_H(m)\to0$ exist on both sides by step 1.1, and their cohomology maps commute with analytification. For $m\ge1$, assume comparison at $m-1$. The lower-dimensional comparison and [F3] give $H^q(H,\mathcal O_H(m))=0$ for $q>0$; the sequence therefore gives analytic higher vanishing at $m$ and an exact sequence on global sections. Every homogeneous degree-$m$ polynomial on $H$ extends by the same polynomial in $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ on $\mathbb P^r$; the kernel of restriction is $x_0$ times the degree-$m-1$ polynomials. The natural map of these exact section sequences is an isomorphism at its outer terms, hence also at its middle term by [F4]. This proves the natural comparison for all $m\ge0$ without using GAGA in dimension $r$.

For the negative twists, the sequence $0\to\mathcal O(-1)\to\mathcal O\to i_*\mathcal O_H\to0$ has restriction $\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ equal to the identity in degree zero and no positive cohomology in the two right terms by [A5] and lower-dimensional comparison. Thus analytic $\mathcal O(-1)$ is acyclic, as is its algebraic counterpart by [F3]. For every $m<-1$, multiplication by a power of $x_0$ injects the line bundle $\mathcal O(m)$ into $\mathcal O(-1)$: in each analytic chart its local equation is a nonzero holomorphic function in the integral holomorphic germ ring, so multiplication is injective. Hence $H^0(\mathcal O(m))=0$. Descend using $0\to\mathcal O(m)\to\mathcal O(m+1)\to i_*\mathcal O_H(m+1)\to0$. Comparison is already known at $m+1$ and on the hyperplane at every twist. For $q\ge1$, the four neighbors in $H^{q-1}(\mathcal O(m+1))\to H^{q-1}(\mathcal O_H(m+1))\to H^q(\mathcal O(m))\to H^q(\mathcal O(m+1))\to H^q(\mathcal O_H(m+1))$ are therefore naturally compared isomorphically, so [F4] gives the middle comparison. This also handles $r=1$, where the point hyperplane's negative twists still have a one-dimensional section space; they were not incorrectly set to zero. Thus all integer twists have canonical cohomology comparison, without analytic Serre duality or an affine finite-pole assertion.

Resolve an algebraic coherent $\mathcal F$ by [F2]. Its finite twisting-sheaf resolution stays exact analytically by step 1.1. Starting at its leftmost term, the long exact sequences and steps 2.1–2.2 prove cohomology comparison for each successive cokernel and hence for $\mathcal F$ in every degree. This uses the actual finite resolution, not an unproved global analytic free resolution.

Let $\mathcal M$ now be any coherent analytic sheaf on $\mathbb P^r$. For every nonzero linear section $s$, retain both $K_s=\ker(\mathcal M(-1)\xrightarrow{s}\mathcal M)$ and $Q_s=\operatorname{coker}(s)$, and write $I_s=\operatorname{im}(s)$. Locally $s$ is a hyperplane equation, so it annihilates $K_s$ and $Q_s$; [A3] makes them coherent sheaves on $H_s\cong\mathbb P^{r-1}$. The inductive equivalence algebraizes them. By [F3], their positive cohomology vanishes after sufficiently positive twists. The two exact sequences $0\to K_s(n)\to\mathcal M(n-1)\to I_s(n)\to0$ and $0\to I_s(n)\to\mathcal M(n)\to Q_s(n)\to0$ then show that multiplication by $s$ on $H^q(\mathcal M(n-1))$ is eventually an isomorphism for $q\ge2$, and eventually surjective for $q=1$. The $H^0(Q_s(n))$ term prevents an initial claim of injectivity in degree one. This argument includes hyperplane torsion; $s$ was not assumed injective on $\mathcal M$.

For finitely presented algebraic $\mathcal F$, a finite presentation computes the sheaf $\mathcal H om(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ as a kernel between finite powers of $\mathcal G$. Exact analytification and [A3] therefore identify its analytification with analytic $\mathcal H om(\mathcal F^{an},\mathcal G^{an})$. Step 4.1 in degree zero identifies morphisms. A finite locally free resolution of $\mathcal F$ computes global $\operatorname{Ext}^q$ by the hypercohomology of its Hom complex: locally free Hom is exact, and an injective resolution gives the resulting double-complex comparison. Termwise cohomology comparison and finiteness of the resolution identify algebraic and analytic Ext in every degree. Thus full faithfulness and cohomology/Ext comparison in dimension $r$ are proved before essential surjectivity.

Fix $q>0$ and a nonzero $s_0$. For $q=1$, the eventual surjections in step 4.2 make the finite dimensions in [A4] nonincreasing integers, hence eventually constant; thereafter multiplication by $s_0$ is an isomorphism. For $q\ge2$ it is already eventually an isomorphism. Choose $N$ beyond this range, put $V=H^q(\mathcal M(N))$, and identify each $H^q(\mathcal M(n))$, $n\ge N$, with $V$ by successive multiplication by $s_0$. A second independent section $s_1$ induces an endomorphism $T_n$ on $V$ between successive degrees. The commuting multiplication square gives $T_{n+1}=T_n=T$. If $V\ne0$, choose an eigenvalue $\lambda$ by [F7]. Multiplication by the nonzero section $s_1-\lambda s_0$ then induces $T-\lambda I$, singular at every such degree. But step 4.2 applied to this fixed section is eventually an isomorphism for $q\ge2$; for $q=1$ it is eventually surjective between spaces of the same stabilized dimension and hence an isomorphism too. This contradiction proves eventual vanishing. The eigenvalue is chosen before its section's threshold; no bound uniform over an infinite pencil is used.

A simultaneous bound is available. For $1\le q\le r$ take the maximum of the finitely many bounds from step 5.2. If $q>r$, the inductive algebraic dimension bound [F7] makes all relevant cohomology groups of $K_s,Q_s$ in step 4.2 zero at every twist. Multiplication by every nonzero $s$ is then an isomorphism on $H^q(\mathcal M(n))$ at every integer $n$. The same two-section contradiction starting at any degree forces these groups to be zero at every twist. Thus one integer bounds vanishing for all $q>0$.

Fix a point $p$ and choose a hyperplane $H_s$ through it. By the inductive equivalence, $Q_s$ is algebraic. Its finite resolution [F2] begins with a surjection from a finite sum of twisting sheaves. After a sufficiently positive twist each summand is generated by its finite homogeneous monomials, so $Q_s(n)$ has finitely many global generators, analytically as well by inductive comparison. Also choose $n$ so $H^1(\mathcal M(n-1))=0$ by step 6.1 and $H^2(K_s(n))=0$ by induction and [F3]. The first exact sequence in step 4.2 gives $H^1(I_s(n))=0$; the second then lifts those finitely many generators to global sections of $\mathcal M(n)$. The cokernel $C$ of these lifts satisfies $C_p/sC_p=0$, so local Nakayama [F7] gives $C_p=0$. Finite local generation of the coherent cokernel gives an open neighborhood of $p$ on which the lifts generate.

Shrink each such neighborhood into a coordinate nonvanishing set $\{\ell_p\ne0\}$, with generating sections of some twist $n_p$. Compactness gives finitely many neighborhoods $U_j$ covering projective space, with integers $n_j$. For every $n\ge\max_j n_j$, multiply the $j$th generating set by $\ell_j^{n-n_j}$. These are global sections of $\mathcal M(n)$ and still generate on $U_j$, since $\ell_j$ is a unit there. Their finite union generates everywhere. This proves analytic positive-twist generation from the exact earlier suppliers. No assertion about finite pole order of arbitrary entire functions on an affine chart is used.

Apply step 8.1 to $\mathcal M$ to obtain a surjection $\mathcal O(-a)^u\to\mathcal M$. Its kernel is coherent by [A3], so a second application gives a finite presentation of $\mathcal M$ by sums of twisting sheaves. By step 2.1 every matrix entry is an algebraic section of the corresponding twisting line bundle. Take its algebraic cokernel; step 1.1 identifies its analytification with $\mathcal M$. Step 5.1 algebraizes each isomorphism and its inverse and preserves their identity composites. $X=\mathbb P^n_k$ with dualizing line bundle $\omega_X=\mathcal O(-n-1)$ and
residue trace $t_X:H^n(X,\omega_X)\to k$
([[def-smooth-projective-dualizing-line-bundle-and-trace]]), and let
$\operatorname{Ext}^q_{\mathcal O_X}$ be the global sheaf Ext of
[[def-sheaf-ext-for-coherent-modules]].

1. **(The pairing.)** For every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$, every
   $q\in\{0,\dots,n\}$, $\alpha\in\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)$
   and $\eta\in H^q(X,F)$ set
   $$\langle\alpha,\eta\rangle_F\;:=\;t_X\Bigl(\chi^n_{\omega_X}\bigl(\alpha\cdot\chi^q_F{}^{-1}(\eta)\bigr)\Bigr),$$
   where $\chi^q_F:\operatorname{Ext}^q_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X,F)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^q(X,F)$
   is the canonical isomorphism of
   [[lem-injective-modules-flasque-and-ext-of-structure-sheaf]],
   $\chi^q_F{}^{-1}(\eta)$ is the corresponding class in
   $\operatorname{Ext}^q_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X,F)$, and
   $\alpha\cdot\beta\in\operatorname{Ext}^n_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X,\omega_X)$
   is the Yoneda product of
   $\alpha\in\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)$ with
   $\beta=\chi^q_F{}^{-1}(\eta)$, i.e. composition
   $\alpha\circ\beta$ of derived morphisms under
   $\operatorname{Ext}^{\bullet}_{\mathcal O_X}(-,-)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X))}(-,-[\bullet])$
   ([[thm-ext-is-hom-in-the-derived-category]],
   [[prop-yoneda-product-is-composition-in-the-derived-category]]). This

2. **(Perfectness.)** For every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$ and every
   $q\in\{0,\dots,n\}$ the pairing
   $$\langle-,-\rangle_F:\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)\times H^q(X,F)\longrightarrow k$$
   is a perfect pairing of $k$-vector spaces, i.e. both adjoint maps
   $\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)\to H^q(X,F)^\vee$ and
   $H^q(X,F)\to\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)^\vee$ are

Let $A$ be a framed unitary ASD connection on the round oriented $S^4$, let $\mathcal E$ be its Ward bundle on $Z=\mathbb CP^3$, and let $k=-q_N(A)$. $$H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))=H^1(Z,\mathcal E^\vee(-2))=0.$$

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z\otimes K\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

whose middle cohomology is $\mathcal E$ and whose terms are

$$U=H^2(Z,\mathcal E(-3)),\qquad K=H^2(Z,\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2),\qquad U'=H^2(Z,\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1)),$$

with $\dim U=\dim U'=k$ and $\dim K=2k+N$. The construction is natural in framed bundle isomorphisms and unique up to changes of bases in $U,K,U'$. The values of all global parallel sections form its maximal trivial flat parallel summand, and the connection splits orthogonally into that summand and a summand with no nonzero parallel sections; arbitrary nonflat parallel summands are permitted. The monad construction is additive across this splitting and uses no hypothesis $H^0(Z,\mathcal E)=0$.

Fix integers $N\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ and standard Hermitian spaces $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$. A framed ADHM linear datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$ and $J:V\to W$. Define the complex and real polynomial expressions

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, with $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$ and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable if there is no nonzero subspace of $V$ invariant under both $B_i$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular if it is stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. Its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$.

Write $X^s=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable}\}$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in X^s:x\text{ costable}\}$ and, for real $\zeta\ge0$, $X_\zeta^U=\{x\in X^s:\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=\zeta I_V\}$. Denote the corresponding orbit sets by $X^s/GL(V)$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V)$ and $X_\zeta^U/U(V)$, with quotient topologies when discussing their analytic spaces. A word frame consists of $k$ columns obtained by fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard basis vectors of $W$.

For $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^2\times(\mathbb C^*)^N$, write $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N$ for the coordinate characters and put $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot x=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$. The compact torus is its subgroup on which all characters have modulus one. The framing representation thus has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$.

These are finite-dimensional matrix definitions. They do not assert a real/complex quotient correspondence, a sheaf or ASD identification, or a noncompact pushforward. In particular, positive-FI stability and zero-FI regularity are distinct conditions; neither an endpoint identification nor an ordinary ASD interpretation follows from this definition.

Give $S^4$ the round metric and the orientation specified in the definition of the framed ASD sector, and assume $F_A^+=0$. Then the induced determinant-line connection on $\det E=\Lambda^N E$ is flat. Its framing at $\infty$ determines a unique global unit parallel section, so the framed unitary bundle reduces to a framed $SU(N)$ bundle. With $q_N=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A)$ and the determinant Chern-form convention $c(A)=\det(I-F_A/(2\pi i))$, one has

$$q_N(E,A)=-\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle\in-\mathbb Z_{\geq0}.$$

Thus $k=-q_N=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle$ is a nonnegative integer, with the sign corresponding to the anti-self-dual equation $F_A^+=0$.

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional Hausdorff
second-countable smooth manifold, possibly with boundary or empty, and let
$\rho_M:H^*(M;\mathbb Z)\to H^*(M;\mathbb R)$ be induced by
$\mathbb Z\hookrightarrow\mathbb R$. Write $J_M$ for the natural de Rham
isomorphism from real de Rham cohomology to singular cohomology with real
coefficients.

For every finite-rank smooth complex bundle $E\to M$ with a Hermitian metric
and Hermitian connection $\nabla$, and every $j\geq0$,
$$J_M([c_j(\nabla)])=\rho_M(c_j(E)).$$
For every finite-rank smooth real bundle $V\to M$ with any real connection
$D$, and every $j\geq0$,
$$J_M([p_j(D)])=\rho_M(p_j(V)).$$
For every oriented Euclidean bundle $W\to M$ of even rank with a
metric-compatible connection $\nabla$, and its Thom-normalized Euler class,
$$J_M([e(\nabla)])=\rho_M(e(W)).$$
Here $c_j(\nabla)$, $p_j(D)$, and $e(\nabla)$ use the normalizations in
[[def-chern-pontryagin-and-euler-characteristic-forms]], while $c_j(E)$,
$p_j(V)$, and $e(W)$ are the published topological classes. In particular
$c_1(L)=e(L_{\mathbb R})$ for a complex line and
$p_j(V)=(-1)^j c_{2j}(V_{\mathbb C})$. These are equalities after passage to
real coefficients; no equality with integral torsion is asserted.

Assume AC. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$, $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, and let $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ satisfy the raw complex equation $\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. Put $K=V\oplus V\oplus W$. For $z=(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2$ put

$$a_z=(B_1-z_1,B_2-z_2,J)^T,\qquad b_z=(-B_2^\dagger+\bar z_2,B_1^\dagger-\bar z_1,I^\dagger)^T,\qquad D_z=\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\dagger\\a_z^\dagger\end{pmatrix}.$$

Then

$$D_zD_z^\dagger=\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\dagger b_z&\mu_{\mathbb C}\\\mu_{\mathbb C}^\dagger&a_z^\dagger a_z\end{pmatrix},\qquad b_z^\dagger b_z-a_z^\dagger a_z=\mu_{\mathbb R}.$$

The maps $b_z^\dagger$ are onto for every $z$ exactly when the datum is stable; the maps $a_z$ are injective for every $z$ exactly when it is costable. Consequently, when both moments vanish, regularity is equivalent to $D_z$ being onto for every $z$. On this locus $f_z=a_z^\dagger a_z=b_z^\dagger b_z$ is positive definite and

$$P_z=1-D_z^\dagger\operatorname{diag}(f_z^{-1},f_z^{-1})D_z$$

is the smooth orthogonal projection onto a rank-$N$ bundle over $\mathbb R^4$. The projection connection $\nabla=P\,d$ is unitary and satisfies $F^+=0$ for the positive stereographic orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, where $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$.

In homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ on $\mathbb P^3$, put $A=B_1\lambda_1-B_2^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_1$, $C=B_2\lambda_1+B_1^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_2$ and

$$\alpha=(A,C,J\lambda_1+I^\dagger\lambda_2)^T,\qquad\beta=(-C,A,I\lambda_1-J^\dagger\lambda_2).$$

The polynomial identity is $\beta\alpha=\lambda_1^2\mu_{\mathbb C}+\lambda_1\lambda_2\mu_{\mathbb R}-\lambda_2^2\mu_{\mathbb C}^\dagger$. With $\sigma(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$, one has $\beta(v)=\alpha(\sigma v)^\dagger$. The real line over $z$ is $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. For regular zero-moment data these maps form a holomorphic bundle monad, trivial on each real line, with middle cohomology on the line over $z$ canonically $\ker D_z$. Its framing at infinity is $W$. The torus acts on the homogeneous coordinates by $(\lambda_1,t_1t_2\lambda_2,t_1\mu_1,t_2\mu_2)$ and on the raw data by $(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$; the monad isomorphism has source, middle and target factors $(t_1t_2)^{-1}$, $\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)$ and $1$, respectively. It preserves the framing representation $W$ with weights $e_\alpha^{-1}$.

This proves a forward raw block construction. It does not assert that every real Ward monad has this normal form, that its inverse extraction is unique, or that the connection extends with charge $k$; those global correspondence and charge assertions require their separate proofs.

Let $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$, $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, and let $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ satisfy $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$ and be stable, meaning that the vectors obtained by applying all words in $B_1,B_2$ to $I(W)$ span $V$. Costable means that no nonzero common $B_1,B_2$-invariant subspace lies in $\ker J$, and regular means stable and costable. On $\mathbb P^2$ with coordinates $[z_0:z_1:z_2]$, define

$$\alpha=\begin{pmatrix}z_0B_1-z_1\\z_0B_2-z_2\\z_0J\end{pmatrix}:V\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to(V\oplus V\oplus W)\otimes\mathcal O,\qquad \beta=\begin{pmatrix}-z_0B_2+z_2&z_0B_1-z_1&z_0I\end{pmatrix}:(V\oplus V\oplus W)\otimes\mathcal O\to V\otimes\mathcal O(1).$$

Then $\beta\alpha=z_0^2([B_1,B_2]+IJ)=0$, $\alpha$ is injective as a sheaf map, and $\beta$ is surjective at every point. The three-term complex is a monad, meaning it is exact at its first and last terms; its middle cohomology $\mathcal E=\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha$ is torsion-free of rank $N$, has Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$, and has a canonical framing $\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}\cong W\otimes\mathcal O_{L_\infty}$. Every framed torsion-free sheaf with this rank, framing and Hilbert polynomial arises uniquely up to simultaneous change of basis in $V$ from this construction. For a finite-type complex scheme $S$, a family of ADHM data is a rank-$k$ vector bundle with endomorphisms and framing maps satisfying the equation and stable on every geometric fiber; its monad cohomology is flat over $S$, and the two constructions are inverse on those families for which the relative cohomology bundles and base-change maps in the preceding Beilinson lemma have the stated ranks and are isomorphisms. A first-order framed deformation means an isomorphism class of such a family over $\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ with its special fiber identified; the correspondence induces inverse maps on those deformation spaces and their tangent vector spaces. The sheaf is locally free exactly when the ADHM datum is costable; hence the regular locus is the locally-free sheaf locus. Combined with the real/complex quotient theorem, positive-FI data correspond to all such framed torsion-free sheaves, while the zero-FI real quotient corresponds to the locally-free locus. The framing representation has character $\sum_{a=1}^N e_a^{-1}$ and the dual framing has character $\sum_{a=1}^N e_a$.

Fix integers $N\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ and standard Hermitian spaces $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$. A framed ADHM linear datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$ and $J:V\to W$. Define the complex and real polynomial expressions

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, with $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$ and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable if there is no nonzero subspace of $V$ invariant under both $B_i$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular if it is stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. Its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$.

Write $X^s=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable}\}$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in X^s:x\text{ costable}\}$ and, for real $\zeta\ge0$, $X_\zeta^U=\{x\in X^s:\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=\zeta I_V\}$. Denote the corresponding orbit sets by $X^s/GL(V)$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V)$ and $X_\zeta^U/U(V)$, with quotient topologies when discussing their analytic spaces. A word frame consists of $k$ columns obtained by fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard basis vectors of $W$.

For $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^2\times(\mathbb C^*)^N$, write $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N$ for the coordinate characters and put $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot x=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$. The compact torus is its subgroup on which all characters have modulus one. The framing representation thus has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$.

These are finite-dimensional matrix definitions. They do not assert a real/complex quotient correspondence, a sheaf or ASD identification, or a noncompact pushforward. In particular, positive-FI stability and zero-FI regularity are distinct conditions; neither an endpoint identification nor an ordinary ASD interpretation follows from this definition.

Fix integers $N\geq2$ and $k\geq0$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian inner products. A raw framed ADHM datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$. Its complex and real moment expressions are

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable when the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, for $m\geq0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$, and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable when no nonzero subspace of $V$ is invariant under both $B_1,B_2$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular when it is both stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ and its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$. The regular zero-FI real quotient is the orbit set

$$\mathcal A^{\mathrm{reg}}_{k,N}=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable and costable}\}/U(V).$$

Let $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ have the unit round metric and the orientation whose restriction to the stereographic coordinates $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$ on $\mathbb R^4=S^4\setminus\{\infty\}$ is $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$. For a smooth right principal $U(N)$-bundle $P\to S^4$, let $E=P\times_{U(N)}\mathbb C^N$ be its Hermitian associated vector bundle, let $A$ be a smooth unitary connection, and let $\Phi:E|_{\infty}\to\mathbb C^N$ be a unitary framing. Write $F_A$ for the anti-Hermitian curvature matrix and define

$$q_N(P,A)=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A).$$

The anti-self-dual equation is $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2=0$. For integer $k\geq0$, the framed ASD sector $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ is the set of such framed connections satisfying $F_A^+=0$ and $q_N(P,A)=-k$, modulo smooth unitary gauge transformations whose value at $\infty$ is the identity in the framing. This definition alone does not assert that every sector exists or that $q_N$ is integral; the exact $U(N)$ charge normalization is a separate lemma below.

Identify $\mathbb H^2$ with $\mathbb C^4$ using a fixed right quaternionic structure $j$ with $j^2=-1$. The twistor space is $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)$, the projection $\pi:Z\to\mathbb H\mathbb P^1=S^4$ sends a complex line $\ell$ to the quaternionic line $\ell+j\ell$, and the antiholomorphic involution is $\sigma([v])=[jv]$. A real twistor line is a fibre $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)\cong\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$; $\sigma$ restricts to the antipodal map on each such line. Fix homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ so $\sigma$ is induced by $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)\mapsto(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$. The finite real line over $z$ has equations $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. These equations fix the quaternionic identification and its orientation. In the chart $\lambda_1=1,\lambda_2=0$, vertical complex orientation followed by the positive orientation of $(z_1,z_2)$ is the complex orientation of $Z$.


For the spinor convention, use the standard spin structure on $S^4$ and $\operatorname{Spin}(4)\cong SU(2)_+\times SU(2)_-$. Let $S^+,S^-$ be the associated rank-two complex spinor bundles, so $T_{\mathbb C}S^4\cong S^+\otimes S^-$. The twistor fibre at $x$ is $\mathbb P(S_x^+)$, and the complex two-plane associated with $\ell\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ is $\ell\otimes S_x^-$. Use the Levi-Civita connection of the round metric for the horizontal distribution of $\pi$; the horizontal $(0,1)$ subspace at $[\ell]\in L_x$ projects to this complex alpha-plane. The displayed orientation is the twistor orientation: the vertical complex orientation followed by the quotient orientation on $S^4$ agrees with the complex orientation on $Z$. It is chosen so the curvature component that vanishes on every such plane is precisely $F^+=(F+*_gF)/2$. In spinor components, $F_{AB}=F_{(AB)}$ denotes the symmetric spinor corresponding to $F^+$ under $\Lambda^2_+T_x^*S^4\otimes\mathbb C\cong\operatorname{Sym}^2(S_x^+)^*$; restriction to the plane is $F_{AB}\pi^A\pi^B$, which vanishes for every $[\pi]\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ exactly when $F^+=0$.

A linear monad on $Z$ is a complex of holomorphic bundles

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal O_Z\otimes K\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

where $U,U',K$ are finite-dimensional complex vector spaces, $b\circ a=0$, $a$ is injective as a sheaf map, $b$ is surjective, and the cohomology sheaf $\ker b/\operatorname{im}a$ is locally free. It is framed when that cohomology has a specified unitary trivialization on $L_\infty$. For a holomorphic bundle $\mathcal E$ on $Z$ that is holomorphically trivial on every real line, a positive Hermitian Ward reality datum is a holomorphic nondegenerate pairing $b:\mathcal E\otimes\sigma^*\overline{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal O_Z$ satisfying $b_{\sigma z}(v,u)=\overline{b_z(u,v)}$. Here $b_z$ is complex linear in $u\in\mathcal E_z$ and conjugate linear in $v\in\mathcal E_{\sigma z}$; the conjugate pullback is holomorphic because $\sigma$ is antiholomorphic. For holomorphic sections $s,t$ on $L_x$, the function $b_z(s(z),t(\sigma z))$ is holomorphic on the compact line, hence constant. It defines $h_x(s,t)$; require this Hermitian form to be positive definite for every $x$. The metric on each fibre of $\mathcal E|_{L_x}$ is transported from this form by holomorphic evaluation. Thus positive forms are induced by the pairing, not independent arbitrary choices. A framed Ward bundle includes a unitary framing on $L_\infty$ for this induced form. Smoothness and parallelness of the induced section-bundle metric are conclusions of the Ward construction.

The compact torus $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ acts on $\mathbb R^4\cong\mathbb C^2$ by $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(t_1z_1,t_2z_2)$ and on $W$ by $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its raw ADHM action is

$$ (t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ). $$

On the framed ASD sector, the same torus acts by inverse pullback under the indicated rotation of $S^4$ and by postcomposition of the framing with $h$. On $Z$, the rotations act by $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]\mapsto[\lambda_1:t_1t_2\lambda_2:t_1\mu_1:t_2\mu_2]$, equivalently the projective spin lift to $\mathbb P(S^+)$; the central sign in the spin double cover acts trivially after projectivization, and the induced action commutes with $\sigma$. The framing torus acts on the framed monad cohomology by the same diagonal representation.

Let $\pi:Z=\mathbb CP^3\to S^4$ be the oriented twistor fibration with the conventions stated in the following references section, let $H=c_1(\mathcal O_Z(1))$, and let $E\to S^4$ be a framed unitary ASD rank-$N$ bundle whose Ward bundle is $\mathcal E=\pi^*E$ as a smooth bundle. $$\mathcal O_Z(-1)^{\oplus k}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus(2k+N)}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z(1)^{\oplus k}.$$

Then $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=N-kH^2$, $c_1(\mathcal E)=0$, and $c_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$. For the twistor orientation specified in the Definition, if $u\in H^4(S^4;\mathbb Z)$ satisfies $\langle u,[S^4]\rangle=1$, then $\pi^*u=H^2$. Consequently

$$k=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=-q_N(E,A).$$

The two constructions are inverse because each orbit intersection is unique; the quotient map is a diffeomorphism in the word-frame charts. The family and first-order version is conditional on [A2]'s displayed base-change hypotheses and [A3], so no tangent claim is inferred outside that range.

Starting with a framed ASD connection, [A4] constructs its holomorphic Ward bundle; the exact coupled cohomology-vanishing and diagonal argument [[lem-qftx-asd-twistor-vanishing-and-monad-reconstruction]] reconstructs the normalized three-term monad. Starting with regular ADHM data, [A5] identifies its normalized real monad and projection connection with this Ward bundle and connection. $$\mathbf V_{\vec Y}=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha\sum_{(i,j)\in Y_\alpha}t_1^it_2^j.$$
Then $\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N}$ is smooth of complex dimension $2kN$, and its $T$-fixed points are isolated and in bijection with the $N$-tuples of partitions of total size $k$. At the fixed point $\vec Y$, the tangent character is
$$\operatorname{ch}_T(T_{\vec Y}\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N})=\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf V_{\vec Y}(t_1+t_2-1-t_1t_2)+\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf W^\vee+t_1t_2\mathbf W\mathbf V_{\vec Y}.$$
For each character $\chi$, let $u_\chi=c_1^T(\chi)$. Let $E_{\vec Y}$ be the product of $u_\chi$ over the tangent weights counted with multiplicity; the fixed points are isolated, so none of these weights is zero. Define the fixed-point series by
$$Z^{\mathrm{fp}}_N(q)=\sum_{k\geq0}q^k\sum_{|\vec Y|=k}E_{\vec Y}^{-1}\in K\langle\!\langle q\rangle\!\rangle.$$
Each coefficient is a finite sum, and the series is formal; no analytic convergence is asserted.

Assume full AC as inherited from the supplied instanton-charge convention. If a $T$-equivariant isomorphism from the positive-FI quotient to the moduli of framed rank-$N$ torsion-free coherent sheaves on $\mathbb{CP}^2$ with Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$ is supplied, it transfers the fixed-point classification and tangent characters to that Gieseker space. If a separately proved noncompact equivariant pushforward for $\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N}$ has a localization identity with these isolated fixed points and tangent Euler classes, then its value on the unit is the coefficient displayed above. Work in $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}$. Let $T$ be a compact torus acting smoothly on a compact oriented smooth $n$-manifold $M$ without boundary; use the standard Hausdorff, second-countable manifold convention, and assume the action preserves the orientation. Write $F=M^T=\coprod_{j=1}^{s}F_j$ for its fixed locus, with $s<\infty$, and $i_j:F_j\hookrightarrow M$ for each connected component. Give each normal bundle $\nu_j$ a $T$-equivariant orientation and orient $F_j$ by $o(TM|_{F_j})=o(TF_j)\wedge o(\nu_j)$. Use real Borel equivariant cohomology, $\mathcal R=H^*(BT;\mathbb R)$, the multiplicative set $S$ generated by nonzero character classes, and the degree-shifting fiber-integration convention of the preceding definition. For every homogeneous $\alpha\in H_T^k(M;\mathbb R)$,

$$\int_M\alpha=\sum_j\int_{F_j}\frac{i_j^*\alpha}{e_T(\nu_j)}\quad\text{in }S^{-1}H^{k-n}(BT;\mathbb R).$$

If the fixed locus is nonempty and consists of isolated points, necessarily $n=2m$. Use the ambient orientation on each normal space $\nu_p=T_pM$ and the positive orientation on each point $p$. Choose a $T$-invariant complex structure on each $T_pM$ and let $\chi_{p,1},\ldots,\chi_{p,m}$ be its nonzero character weights. Let $\epsilon_p=+1$ when its complex orientation agrees with the orientation of $M$ at $p$ and $-1$ otherwise. Then the same formula specializes to

$$\int_M\alpha=\sum_{p\in M^T}\frac{\epsilon_p\,i_p^*\alpha}{\prod_{a=1}^{m}u_{\chi_{p,a}}}\quad\text{in }S^{-1}\mathcal R.$$

If the fixed locus is empty, the fixed-component formula is the empty sum $0$ for every $n$; no parity condition or integer $m$ is needed in that case.

This is a finite-dimensional formula for compact manifolds; it does not assert a formula for arbitrary noncompact instanton spaces or infinite-dimensional field spaces.

Assume full AC. Fix integers $N\geq1$ and $k\geq0$ and a positive real stability parameter $\zeta$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ have their standard Hermitian structures. Define $\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N}$ to be the geometric quotient by $GL(V)$ of data $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I\in\operatorname{Hom}(W,V)$, $J\in\operatorname{Hom}(V,W)$, $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$, and $\operatorname{span}\{B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w):m\geq0,\ w\in W\}=V$. The positive parameter $\zeta$ specifies the positive-FI stability chamber. Let $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$, with rotation characters $t_1,t_2$ and dual framing characters $e_1,\ldots,e_N$. Thus $W$ has character $\mathbf W=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and $W^\vee$ has character $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$, where $h$ acts on $W$ with weights $e_\alpha^{-1}$. Work over the rational function field $K=\mathbb Q(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,a_1,\ldots,a_N)$ in algebraically independent variables. For $\chi=t_1^{m_1}t_2^{m_2}\prod_\alpha e_\alpha^{n_\alpha}$ set $u_\chi=m_1\epsilon_1+m_2\epsilon_2+\sum_\alpha n_\alpha a_\alpha$.

For a partition $Y$, a Young diagram means a finite downward-closed subset of $\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^2$; write $|Y|$ for its number of boxes. For an $N$-tuple $\vec Y=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_N)$ set $|\vec Y|=\sum_\alpha|Y_\alpha|$, $\mathbf W=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$, $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$, and
$$\mathbf V_{\vec Y}=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha\sum_{(i,j)\in Y_\alpha}t_1^it_2^j.$$
Then $\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N}$ is smooth of complex dimension $2kN$, and its $T$-fixed points are isolated and in bijection with the $N$-tuples of partitions of total size $k$. At the fixed point $\vec Y$, the tangent character is
$$\operatorname{ch}_T(T_{\vec Y}\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N})=\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf V_{\vec Y}(t_1+t_2-1-t_1t_2)+\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf W^\vee+t_1t_2\mathbf W\mathbf V_{\vec Y}.$$
Let $E_{\vec Y}$ be the product of $u_\chi$ over the tangent weights counted with multiplicity; the fixed points are isolated, so none of these weights is zero. Define the fixed-point series by
$$Z^{\mathrm{fp}}_N(q)=\sum_{k\geq0}q^k\sum_{|\vec Y|=k}E_{\vec Y}^{-1}\in K\langle\!\langle q\rangle\!\rangle.$$
Each coefficient is a finite sum, and the series is formal; no analytic convergence is asserted.

The quotient is a separated smooth finite-type complex algebraic variety with a finite invariant affine word-slice atlas for the algebraic complex torus $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^{N+2}$. This result concerns the stable matrix quotient and a formal series. It asserts no sheaf/ASD dictionary or integration identity.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $N\geq 2$ and let $S^4=\mathbb R^4\cup\{\infty\}$ be the one-point compactification, oriented so the coordinates $x^1,x^2,x^3,x^4$ on $\mathbb R^4$ have $dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\wedge dx^4>0$. Give $S^4$ a smooth round metric in the conformal class of the Euclidean metric on $\mathbb R^4$. A framed $U(N)$ connection is a smooth unitary connection $A$ on a Hermitian rank-$N$ vector bundle $E\to S^4$, together with a chosen unitary frame $\Phi:E_\infty\to\mathbb C^N$ of its fiber at $\infty$. Gauge transformations are smooth unitary bundle automorphisms that equal the identity in this frame at $\infty$. The curvature is $F_A$, and the Hodge operator is defined by $\alpha\wedge *_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,d\mathrm{vol}_g$ on two-forms. Set $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2$ and $F_A^-=(F_A-*_gF_A)/2$; the anti-self-dual condition is $F_A^+=0$, and the self-dual condition is $F_A^-=0$.

Let $\mathfrak u(N)$ be the anti-Hermitian matrices and put $B_N(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_N(XY)$. In the trace convention of the library, the charge of $A$ is $q_N(A)=(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}B_N(F_A\wedge F_A)$, and the positive anti-self-dual instanton number is $k(A)=-q_N(A)$. For $k\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}$, the framed anti-self-dual charge-$k$ moduli set $\mathcal I^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ consists of framed pairs $(E,A)$ with $F_A^+=0$ and $k(A)=k$, modulo the stated based gauge transformations. The integer-charge condition is part of the selected bundle sector; no analytic existence or uniqueness assertion is included in this definition. The trace and Hodge conventions agree with the supplied compact-four-manifold definition of $q_B$; its special $SU(2)$ integrality clause is not used to assert $U(N)$ integrality.

For $k\geq0$, take Hermitian spaces $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$. The ADHM data are
$$B_1,B_2\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V),\qquad I\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(W,V),\qquad J\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(V,W).$$
Their data space is $\mathcal R_{k,N}=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)^2\oplus\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(W,V)\oplus\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(V,W)$, and their complex and real moment-map expressions are
$$\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V),\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V).$$
Here $[X,Y]=XY-YX$, and $\dagger$ is the Hermitian adjoint. The two displayed formulas define maps $\mu_{\mathbb C}:\mathcal R_{k,N}\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ and $\mu_{\mathbb R}:\mathcal R_{k,N}\to\operatorname{Herm}(V)$, where $\mathcal R_{k,N}$ is the stated product of four Hom spaces and $\operatorname{Herm}(V)$ is the real vector space of Hermitian endomorphisms. They are the complex and real ADHM moment-map expressions, with these formulas fixing their normalization. A datum is stable when
$$\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w):m\geq0,\ i_j\in\{1,2\},\ w\in W\}=V,$$
where the word of length zero is the identity. Equivalently, no proper $B_1,B_2$-invariant subspace of $V$ contains $\operatorname{im}I$. The group $GL(V)$ consists of invertible complex-linear endomorphisms, and $U(V)$ is its subgroup preserving the chosen Hermitian inner product. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. For $\zeta>0$, the stable complex ADHM quotient $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{GIT},\zeta}_{k,N}$ is the geometric quotient of $\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \text{stable}\}$ by $GL(V)$ in the positive stability chamber; $\zeta$ labels that chamber and is not an additional coordinate on the complex equation set.

For a real parameter $\zeta\geq0$, the real moment-map presentation is the quotient of $\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta\,\mathrm{id}_V,\ \text{stable}\}$ by $U(V)$. At $\zeta>0$ this is called the resolved or positive-FI ADHM quotient; at $\zeta=0$ its affine completion includes the small-instanton locus. The equations and quotient are definitions; this item does not assert that the real moment-map quotient is isomorphic to the stable complex quotient or to an instanton moduli space.

Write $\mathbb{CP}^2$ for the complex projective plane, $\ell_\infty=\{[0:z_1:z_2]\}$ for its line at infinity, and $\mathcal O_{\ell_\infty}$ for the sheaf of holomorphic functions on that line. The affine chart $\mathbb{CP}^2\setminus\ell_\infty$ is $\mathbb C^2$; projective compactification adds the whole line $\ell_\infty$, unlike the one-point compactification $S^4$. Let $\mathcal O(1)$ be the hyperplane line bundle and $\mathcal O(m)=\mathcal O(1)^{\otimes m}$ for $m\geq0$. A coherent sheaf is a sheaf of $\mathcal O_{\mathbb{CP}^2}$-modules that is locally finitely presented; it is torsion-free when no nonzero local section is annihilated by a nonzero local function. Its rank is the dimension of its generic fiber over the function field. Define its Hilbert polynomial by $P_E(m)=\sum_{i=0}^2(-1)^i\dim_{\mathbb C}H^i(\mathbb{CP}^2,E\otimes\mathcal O(m))$ for all sufficiently large integers $m$. The framed Gieseker moduli space $\mathcal G_{k,N}$ is the moduli of pairs $(E,\Phi)$ with $E$ a rank-$N$ torsion-free coherent sheaf, $P_E(m)=N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$, and $\Phi:E|_{\ell_\infty}\cong\mathcal O_{\ell_\infty}^{\oplus N}$. Its locally-free locus is distinguished from the boundary of non-locally-free sheaves. The Uhlenbeck set-theoretic compactification is the disjoint union of strata $\mathcal I^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k-\ell,N}\times\operatorname{Sym}^{\ell}(\mathbb R^4)$ for $0\leq\ell\leq k$, where $\operatorname{Sym}^{\ell}(\mathbb R^4)=(\mathbb R^4)^\ell/S_\ell$ records ideal point defects. The Gieseker space and the Uhlenbeck space are distinct: the former retains torsion-free sheaf data at the small-instanton boundary, while the latter records only ideal points. No compactness of either full space is asserted here.

Write $z_1=x^1+ix^2$ and $z_2=x^3+ix^4$. The compact torus $T=(S^1)^2\times T_G$, with $T_G\subset U(W)$ the diagonal framing torus, acts on ADHM data by
$$(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ).$$
This convention makes $\mu_{\mathbb C}$ transform with character $t_1t_2$ and leaves $\mu_{\mathbb R}$ invariant. Let $e_\alpha$ denote the character of the dual of the $\alpha$th framing line, so the framing representation has character $\mathbf W=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha$. For the rotation characters write $t_1,t_2$, and write $\epsilon_i=c_1^T(t_i)$ and $a_\alpha=c_1^T(e_\alpha)$ for their additive equivariant weights.

Fix integers $N\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ and standard Hermitian spaces $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$. A framed ADHM linear datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$ and $J:V\to W$. Define the complex and real polynomial expressions

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, with $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$ and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable if there is no nonzero subspace of $V$ invariant under both $B_i$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular if it is stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. Its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$.

Write $X^s=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable}\}$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in X^s:x\text{ costable}\}$ and, for real $\zeta\ge0$, $X_\zeta^U=\{x\in X^s:\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=\zeta I_V\}$. Denote the corresponding orbit sets by $X^s/GL(V)$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V)$ and $X_\zeta^U/U(V)$, with quotient topologies when discussing their analytic spaces. A word frame consists of $k$ columns obtained by fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard basis vectors of $W$.

For $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^2\times(\mathbb C^*)^N$, write $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N$ for the coordinate characters and put $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot x=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$. The compact torus is its subgroup on which all characters have modulus one. The framing representation thus has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$.

These are finite-dimensional matrix definitions. They do not assert a real/complex quotient correspondence, a sheaf or ASD identification, or a noncompact pushforward. In particular, positive-FI stability and zero-FI regularity are distinct conditions; neither an endpoint identification nor an ordinary ASD interpretation follows from this definition.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$, $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, and let $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ satisfy $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$ and be stable, meaning that the vectors obtained by applying all words in $B_1,B_2$ to $I(W)$ span $V$. Costable means that no nonzero common $B_1,B_2$-invariant subspace lies in $\ker J$, and regular means stable and costable. On $\mathbb P^2$ with coordinates $[z_0:z_1:z_2]$, define

$$\alpha=\begin{pmatrix}z_0B_1-z_1\\z_0B_2-z_2\\z_0J\end{pmatrix}:V\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to(V\oplus V\oplus W)\otimes\mathcal O,\qquad \beta=\begin{pmatrix}-z_0B_2+z_2&z_0B_1-z_1&z_0I\end{pmatrix}:(V\oplus V\oplus W)\otimes\mathcal O\to V\otimes\mathcal O(1).$$

Then $\beta\alpha=z_0^2([B_1,B_2]+IJ)=0$, $\alpha$ is injective as a sheaf map, and $\beta$ is surjective at every point. The three-term complex is a monad, meaning it is exact at its first and last terms; its middle cohomology $\mathcal E=\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha$ is torsion-free of rank $N$, has Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$, and has a canonical framing $\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}\cong W\otimes\mathcal O_{L_\infty}$. Every framed torsion-free sheaf with this rank, framing and Hilbert polynomial arises uniquely up to simultaneous change of basis in $V$ from this construction. For a finite-type complex scheme $S$, a family of ADHM data is a rank-$k$ vector bundle with endomorphisms and framing maps satisfying the equation and stable on every geometric fiber; its monad cohomology is flat over $S$, and the two constructions are inverse on those families for which the relative cohomology bundles and base-change maps in the preceding Beilinson lemma have the stated ranks and are isomorphisms. A first-order framed deformation means an isomorphism class of such a family over $\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ with its special fiber identified; the correspondence induces inverse maps on those deformation spaces and their tangent vector spaces. The sheaf is locally free exactly when the ADHM datum is costable; hence the regular locus is the locally-free sheaf locus. Combined with the real/complex quotient theorem, positive-FI data correspond to all such framed torsion-free sheaves, while the zero-FI real quotient corresponds to the locally-free locus. The framing representation has character $\sum_{a=1}^N e_a^{-1}$ and the dual framing has character $\sum_{a=1}^N e_a$.
